name: Psalms
lede: The nineteenth book of the Bible, in full: the hundred and fifty psalms in their five books — the blessed man and the tree by the streams, the heavens declaring the glory of God, Jehovah my shepherd, the hart panting after the water brooks, the harps hung on the willows, the songs of ascents and the last great hallelujahs — every word in the words of the ASV.

books.name: Blessed Is the Man
books.blurb: Book I opens: the blessed man like a tree planted by the streams of water, and the wicked like the chaff; why do the nations rage — thou art my son; I laid me down and slept; in the morning will I order my prayer; every night make I my bed to swim; when I consider thy heavens, what is man?; the lurking lion and the net; and the words of Jehovah, pure words, as silver tried in a furnace.

books.name: The Heavens Declare
books.blurb: How long, O Jehovah?; the fool hath said in his heart, There is no God; who shall sojourn in thy tabernacle?; the lines are fallen unto me in pleasant places; hide me under the shadow of thy wings; Jehovah is my rock and my fortress — the cords of death, the earth that shook, the large place; the heavens declare the glory of God; some trust in chariots; and my God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?

books.name: Jehovah Is My Shepherd
books.blurb: Jehovah is my shepherd; I shall not want — green pastures, still waters, the valley of the shadow of death, a table before me; lift up your heads, O ye gates; Jehovah is my light and my salvation; the voice of Jehovah breaketh the cedars; weeping may tarry for the night, but joy cometh in the morning; into thy hand I commend my spirit; blessed is he whose transgression is forgiven; and sing unto him a new song.

books.name: Wait for Jehovah
books.blurb: The close of Book I: O taste and see that Jehovah is good; the angel of Jehovah encampeth round about them that fear him; with thee is the fountain of life — in thy light shall we see light; fret not thyself because of evil-doers; I have been young, and now am old; every man walketh in a vain show; I waited patiently for Jehovah, and he brought me up out of a horrible pit; and blessed be Jehovah, the God of Israel, from everlasting and to everlasting.

books.name: As the Hart Panteth
books.blurb: Book II opens with the sons of Korah: as the hart panteth after the water brooks; deep calleth unto deep; oh send out thy light and thy truth; the king's wedding song and the queen in gold of Ophir; God is our refuge and strength — there is a river, the streams whereof make glad the city of God; be still, and know that I am God; walk about Zion; man that is in honor abideth not; and Asaph: every beast of the forest is mine, and the cattle upon a thousand hills.

books.name: A Clean Heart
books.blurb: Have mercy upon me, O God — purify me with hyssop, and I shall be clean; create in me a clean heart; I am like a green olive-tree in the house of God; oh that I had wings like a dove!; put thou my tears into thy bottle; in the cave — be thou exalted, O God, above the heavens; they go round about the city like dogs; Moab is my washpot; lead me to the rock that is higher than I; and my soul waiteth in silence for God only.

books.name: Let God Arise
books.blurb: My soul thirsteth for thee in a dry and weary land; thy lovingkindness is better than life; thou visitest the earth, and waterest it — the pastures are clothed with flocks; he turned the sea into dry land; God be merciful unto us, and bless us; and let God arise, let his enemies be scattered — the chariots of God, the singers before, the damsels playing with timbrels.

books.name: He Shall Have Dominion
books.blurb: The close of Book II: save me, O God, for the waters are come in unto my soul; make haste to help me; now also when I am old and grayheaded, forsake me not; and Solomon's psalm — he shall come down like rain upon the mown grass, he shall have dominion from sea to sea, the kings of Sheba and Seba shall offer gifts. The prayers of David the son of Jesse are ended.

books.name: Whom Have I in Heaven
books.blurb: Book III opens with Asaph: until I went into the sanctuary of God — whom have I in heaven but thee?; they have set thy sanctuary on fire; in the hand of Jehovah there is a cup; in Salem is his tabernacle; the waters saw thee, O God; and the dark sayings of old — the sea divided, the rock cleft in the wilderness, bread from heaven, the wonders in the field of Zoan, and David taken from the sheepfolds.

books.name: How Amiable Are Thy Tabernacles
books.blurb: The close of Book III: they have laid Jerusalem in heaps; give ear, O Shepherd of Israel — thou broughtest a vine out of Egypt; blow the trumpet at the new moon; God standeth in the congregation of God; they are confederate against thee; how amiable are thy tabernacles — the sparrow hath found her a house; mercy and truth are met together; glorious things are spoken of thee, O city of God; Heman's cry from the lowest pit; and I will sing of the lovingkindness of Jehovah for ever.

books.name: Our Dwelling-place
books.blurb: Book IV opens with the prayer of Moses: Lord, thou hast been our dwelling-place in all generations — a thousand years in thy sight are but as yesterday; he that dwelleth in the secret place of the Most High; it is a good thing to give thanks; the floods have lifted up their voice; oh come, let us sing unto Jehovah; sing unto Jehovah a new song; Jehovah reigneth; he sitteth above the cherubim; and make a joyful noise unto Jehovah, all ye lands.

books.name: Bless Jehovah, O My Soul
books.blurb: I will sing of lovingkindness and justice; I am like a pelican of the wilderness, a sparrow alone upon the housetop; bless Jehovah, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits — thy youth is renewed like the eagle; and O Jehovah, how manifold are thy works — the springs in the valleys, the birds among the branches, the wild goats, the moon for seasons, the sea great and wide, and leviathan.

books.name: He Remembered His Covenant
books.blurb: The close of Book IV: he hath remembered his covenant for ever — unto thee will I give the land of Canaan; Joseph laid in chains of iron; the wonders in the land of Ham; he brought them forth with silver and gold, and spread a cloud for a covering; and we have sinned with our fathers — the Red Sea, the calf in Horeb, Baal-peor — yet he regarded their distress. Blessed be Jehovah, the God of Israel.

books.name: They That Go Down to the Sea
books.blurb: Book V opens: let the redeemed of Jehovah say so — the wanderers, the prisoners, the sick, they that go down to the sea in ships and the storm made a calm; awake, psaltery and harp; Jehovah saith unto my Lord, Sit thou at my right hand; when Israel went forth out of Egypt the mountains skipped like rams; not unto us, O Jehovah; I love Jehovah, because he heareth my voice; and the stone which the builders rejected is become the head of the corner.

books.name: Thy Word Is a Lamp
books.blurb: Psalm 119, the long acrostic, in its twenty-two sections from Aleph to Tav: blessed are they that are perfect in the way; wherewith shall a young man cleanse his way?; I am a sojourner in the earth; for ever, O Jehovah, thy word is settled in heaven; oh how love I thy law!; thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and light unto my path; I rejoice at thy word, as one that findeth great spoil; I have gone astray like a lost sheep.
